entries.n: Formed from 'by cause', so it can mark the intention of an action as well as the reason for it. Chaucer uses it the same way.
The genuine plural of 'beef', which in French still means the living animal; veal, mutton and pork likewise were animal names.
Shakespeare uses 'in that behalf' to mean 'on that account, for that purpose'.
Used for 'besides', not 'by the side of', which is the more modern sense; from Old English.
This is the spelling of the 1611 edition, altered in modern editions.
From Old English, 'a rod, broom'. Still common as a provincialism.
Hardly bestead means 'placed in difficulty', matching the Hebrew.

entries.m: to put in a place, stow away, dispose of
